findings.text: The routine reconciling availability with an exclude mask is defined with external linkage and signals allocation failure with a negative result versus zero on success, offering a callable request point for isolation updates.

Isolation reconciliation entry accepts a caller provided exclude set, may allocate per CPU work storage plus a scratch mask, serializes against online changes, and does not return until all scheduled target CPU work has completed.

Service of timers belonging to another CPU is bypassed while that CPU is unavailable or already owned for remote service or marked ignoring or while its upcoming expiry is still ahead of the given time.
Upward progress in a group is allowed only for the child currently owning migrator duty, or when no owner is present, with other cases deferred to the existing owner.
Readiness for upward remote work is determined by time reaching the cached group expiry, with that expiry preserved as the walk earliest value and a check flag raised when due.

Parent active membership drops the bit of a child that went idle, and when that child was the owner a successor is picked from leftovers, clearing ownership and demanding further ascent when none remain while always advancing the sequence.
Hierarchy choice follows a capacity key that is forced to a uniform default under full tickless mode or without capacity support, and otherwise varies per CPU by architectural measure.
Level placement favors an existing group sharing the node below the cross node boundary with room for more children, creating a node local group only if no placement candidate qualifies.
Fresh groups begin childless with no owner, empty active membership, initial sequence, drained event queue, and a group event held at the distant future with ignore asserted.
Reconciliation treats newly restored and newly withdrawn CPUs as disjoint phases with unisolate before isolate, and never withdraws a tick CPU that lacks hotplug support.
Becoming available records current idle posture and joins hierarchy activity only when awake, while becoming unavailable parks wakeup far ahead and leaves hierarchy activity with an update.
The cross CPU activation poke assumes the target is both available and awake, acting as a hint to reexamine active state after a peer changed availability.

Refresh of a remote CPU keeps base timer locks ahead of migration locks, retains the per CPU migration lock across retrieval of the upcoming remote interrupt, and drops base locks ahead of hierarchy traversal to shrink the combined hold.
Ownership of remote expiry is performed without holding the per CPU migration lock to permit concurrent idle exit by the remote CPU, reacquiring with interrupts suppressed afterwards.
Group level expired work is selected under the group lock, then the lock is released for per CPU service and retaken to snapshot the upcoming expiry before ascent continues.
Availability mask and per CPU availability updates are ordered under a dedicated mutex outer to the per CPU lock, preventing overlapping transitions of the same CPU.
Migrator word changes rely on atomic compare exchange retries with acquire semantics and a barrier after failure, ordered against concurrent activation side changes.
Group search and creation run under a global mutex and new parent links become visible through release publication, so concurrent idle path readers see complete parent initialization.
Both isolation phases run under protection against CPU online changes, with each scheduled target work item flushed before the scratch mask is reused for the following phase.

Observed per CPU migration data includes availability plus idle plus remote ownership indicators, a wakeup instant, an event carrying ignore plus upcoming expiry, hierarchy group linkage plus child mask, and a dedicated lock.

Observed group data includes a lock, level, node affinity, child tally, atomic migrator word, event queue, group event with expiry plus ignore, cached upcoming expiry, parent link, group mask and level linkage.
Observed walk cursor includes upcoming plus earliest expiries, an event link, remote plus check indicators, base jiffies plus current time captures, and the source child mask.
Observed hierarchy container includes a capacity key, CPU membership mask, per level group inventories, a root link and a global registry node for capacity lookup.
Observed migrator word combines an owner mask plus an active membership mask plus a sequence count, allowing single atomic replacement with forward progress detection.
Remote ownership starts before cross CPU expiry and ends after hierarchy refresh, with detours for offline or reawakened CPUs that skip refresh yet still release ownership.
A CPU cycles between available and withdrawn under isolate plus hotplug control, with withdraw and restore each run on the affected CPU through work items.
Owner state follows active membership, persisting while the owner stays active, moving to another active member when the owner idles, and emptying with upward notice when all members idle.

Growth reuses or creates levels from bottom toward top, attaches each level to its parent, optionally carries activation upward from a grafted prior root, and adopts the lone top group as the new root.
Retrieving the upcoming remote interrupt outside the per CPU lock could interleave with the owner leaving idle and refreshing its own timers, so the retrieval stays covered.
Unprotected reads of the cached group expiry risk splitting on 32 bit builds, requiring locked access there, while 64 bit builds can rely on a single atomic read.
Exposing a fresh parent link ahead of complete parent setup could confuse a concurrent idle transition, addressed through ordered publication paired with ordered acquisition on readers.
Opposite activation versus deactivation attempts may collide on the same migrator word, resolved by repeating the atomic update until it wins while keeping child before parent ordering.
Graft work for a prior root performed by the joining CPU itself outside early boot may cause false activation and early use of mask state, so a different online CPU handles preparation.
A withdrawn CPU that still reports a pending expiry without any remaining available peer in its hierarchy reveals a missing always awake handler for that hierarchy.
Identifier KTIME_MAX is the distant future marker meaning no pending wakeup or expiry for wakeup fields, walk expiries and initial group events.
Identifier TMIGR_NONE is the owner value meaning none, applied to fresh groups and to groups whose active membership drained.
Identifiers TMIGR_CHILDREN_PER_GROUP and BIT_CNT cap group breadth and owner search span for placement plus election.
Identifier SCHED_CAPACITY_SCALE is the uniform capacity key applied when per CPU capacity distinction is turned off.
Identifier NUMA_NO_NODE marks levels without node affinity at or above the cross node boundary.
Negative ENOMEM reports work, mask, group or hierarchy allocation shortfalls, while negative EINVAL reports absent hierarchy or missing group linkage for a CPU.
